_comment: C4 regression gate. Consumed by `cmd/piano-distance --thresholds` and by `just gate-c4`.
A number under `max` is ENFORCED: the run fails (exit 2) when the measured metric
exceeds it. A `null` means NOT YET CALIBRATED - the metric is listed so its existence
is visible, but it is deliberately not enforced. Calibrating one later is a one-line
diff (replace the null with a number), not a new file. Any key here that is not a
float64 field of analysis.Metrics is an ERROR, so typos cannot silently disable a gate.
Thresholds are the values measured on 2026-08-21 plus roughly 8-10% headroom. They are
a regression fence, not a quality target: tighten them whenever a fit genuinely improves.
RE-BASELINED 2026-08-21 by the DWG treble-collapse fix. Two thresholds were LOOSENED,
which normally must not happen; the reasoning is in `recorded.note` and is not a
convenience. Two others were tightened in the same pass. Do not loosen anything here
again without an equally explicit reason.
SPECTRAL CAVEAT: spectral_rmse_db is gated as a RAW dB value, which is a real regression
signal. The NORMALISED spectral component is a different matter - at 58.2 dB against
analysis.NormSpectral = 30.0 it is saturated, clamp01 pins it at 1.0, and it therefore
contributes a constant to `score` with no gradient for the optimizer. Every preset in
the repo saturates it (measured population range 51.5-63.7 dB). Re-calibrating
NormSpectral to roughly 70-80 is the fix, but it rewrites every recorded score and so
belongs in a separate, deliberately re-baselined change - not here.

note: Re-baselined on 2026-08-21 after the DWG string core stopped emitting a DC offset.
Before that change the C4 render was dominated by DC, not by audio: measured over the
second second of a held note 60, the DWG bank output had a mean of +0.606 against an
AC RMS of 0.376. The fitted preset was therefore fitted, and this gate calibrated,
against a signal whose largest single component was a modelling defect.
Removing it moves the metrics in both directions, and all four moves are consistent
with the DC having been counted as signal:
time_rmse           0.1104 -> 0.1022  improved, threshold TIGHTENED 0.12  -> 0.112
spectral_rmse_db    58.18  -> 53.03   improved, threshold TIGHTENED 63.5  -> 57.5
envelope_rmse_db     9.008 -> 10.774  worse,    threshold LOOSENED  9.8   -> 11.75
decay_diff_db_per_s  3.177 ->  5.406  worse,    threshold LOOSENED  3.45  ->  5.9
score                0.5194 -> 0.5327 worse by 2.6%, still inside the unchanged 0.57
The envelope and decay terms got worse because the DC was propping the envelope up:
the candidate decay slope goes from -8.9 to -11.2 dB/s against the reference -5.8,
so the model now decays too fast where before a non-decaying offset hid it. That is a
real shortcoming of the model that was previously masked, not one introduced here.
The honest fix for the two loosened numbers is to re-fit the C4 preset against the
corrected core, which is deliberately out of scope for the change that exposed them.
Expect these two to come back down when that happens; tighten them when it does.
Earlier note, still true of the pre-fix baseline: measured against pristine HEAD as
well as the working tree; both gave the identical score, so those numbers were the
behaviour of analysis.Compare and not a regression introduced by the metric work.
Scores recorded before 2026-08 are NOT comparable: analysis/distance.go changed six
times between 2026-02-14 and 2026-08-16 (phase detection, normalisation), so the
0.3839 in assets/presets/fitted-c4-mayfly.json.report.json was produced by a
different metric implementation.
